summary_responses.response: DiffTry is a lightweight, stateless mechanism that improves microservice reliability by assigning different retry limits to different priority classes. By applying class-specific retry budgets at the point of rejection rather than at the queueing or service level, it protects high-value transactions during overload while suppressing retry storms, without requiring overload detection or coordination between services. The authors develop a mathematical model—first for a single service and then generalized to arbitrary networks—to predict rejection rates, throughput, and prioritization effects under DiffTry, proving convergence and (under certain conditions) uniqueness of solutions, as well as monotonic improvement of high-priority success rates with retry limits. Simulations and a real-world Kubernetes deployment validate that DiffTry's measured performance closely matches theoretical predictions, confirming its practical viability as a drop-in service-mesh plugin requiring no application code changes. Compared to existing approaches like centralized overload control, traditional queue-based prioritization, or other retry-storm mitigation techniques, DiffTry uniquely combines priority differentiation with retry-storm suppression in a fully distributed, coordination-free design. Overall, the paper demonstrates that DiffTry can substantially reduce rejection rates and economic damage for high-priority transactions, even under adversarial or incidental overload conditions, while being easy to deploy in real microservice architectures.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) has issued a direct final rule amending its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations under 5 CFR Part 630 to incorporate statutory changes enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The rule broadens FMLA eligibility by counting virtually all civilian federal service, including temporary and intermittent employment, as well as honorable active military service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps, toward the 12-month service requirement. It also clarifies that annual and sick leave earned under non-title 5 authorities may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, and it excludes Veterans Health Administration (VHA) employees covered under a separate leave system (38 U.S.C. 7421) from title 5 FMLA coverage, since they are governed by a parallel FMLA provision under 38 U.S.C. 7425(c). Because paid parental leave (PPL) eligibility depends on meeting FMLA eligibility requirements, these changes also affect PPL eligibility for federal employees. The rule, which codifies guidance previously issued through OPM policy memoranda, will take effect December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a proposed rule instead.
